transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-04
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Avery (Redwood SE), Priya (NovaPay Head of ML), Carlos (NovaPay Platform), Susan (NovaPay CTO), Kenji (NovaPay SRE)

Summary:
Quick sync on POC throughput results after last tuning pass; discussed continuous batching parameters, concurrency targets, and queueing/backpressure; agreed next steps: share detailed benchmark CSV, run on-site perf test, and propose Dedicated pricing for peak capacity.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick context, same agenda as last week, go over the numbers Liam pushed yesterday, then tuning and next steps.

00:18 Speaker 2 (Priya): Thanks Maya, yep we pulled the latest numbers this morning and we also had one of our devs try the new batching config. we saw some uplift but there were some spikes.

00:33 Speaker 3 (Liam): cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, but high level we got continuous-batching enabled with a 20ms max-wait and target batch size of 128 on the 2x A100 nodes you gave us. raw throughput per node increased about 2.6x for our 512-token workloads, p50 latency is up a bit but p95 is within your target when concurrency is capped.

00:54 Speaker 4 (Carlos): wait, 2.6x? that sounds great. what about tail latency — we saw those spikes at like 700ms yesterday which worries us for user-facing paths.

01:11 Speaker 3 (Liam): yeah, the p95 is around 420ms in the controlled runs but when concurrency climbed unexpectedly we saw queueing piling up and p95 jumped near 700ms. that's where queue sizing and backpressure policies come in. we recommended a max-concurrency of 40 per node for that model family.

01:30 Speaker 2 (Priya): can you explain the difference between the 20ms max-wait and batch_timeout? i'm not sure how those interplay with our request patterns.

01:42 Speaker 3 (Liam): sure — max-wait / batch_timeout is the short window the runtime holds a partial batch waiting for more requests; continuous-batching will also do adaptive coalescing so if requests are steady it fills faster. so 20ms is a balance — it increases throughput significantly while keeping added latency small. if you bump to 50ms you squeeze more tokens per batch but add noticeable latency.

02:04 Speaker 5 (Avery): also worth mentioning prefix/KV caching — since a lot of your requests share system prompts, enabling KV cache cut token compute by about 12% in our runs. that helps lower p95 for repeated contexts.

02:20 Speaker 4 (Carlos): hmm we do have a lot of similar prompts in payment flows. what's the memory hit for KV caching? Kenji here was worried about OOMs because our model footprints are big.

02:33 Speaker 6 (Kenji): yeah we already saw one OOM last week when a long sequence ran and reclaimed cache too slowly.

02:41 Speaker 3 (Liam): good callout — KV cache allocates per-request and is reclaimed on eviction. we tuned the cache size to 6GB per model shard for the 2xA100 config; that avoided OOMs in our stress tests but your prod sequences are longer, so we should either reduce shard cache or increase node memory.

03:02 Speaker 2 (Priya): is there an easy knob to reduce batch size when memory pressure spikes? we'd prefer graceful degradation over crashes.

03:12 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes — Redwood runtime supports an autoshrink on memory pressure, it will lower max_batch and degrade to lower concurrency. there's also queue-length based throttling so you can reject or rate-limit low-priority calls. we can demo that in the on-site run.

03:35 Speaker 1 (Maya): quick commercial note — if you need guaranteed capacity (and avoid noisy neighbor problems), Dedicated pools are the path, we'll include pricing and expected unit economics in the follow-up.

03:46 Speaker 4 (Susan): good, let's see cost first, but reliability is key. for a payment infra we can't have those spikes.

04:00 Speaker 3 (Liam): understood. i want to walk through the numbers briefly — i'll call out some imperfect transcriptions from the run but try to keep it accurate. the baseline run without continuous-batching was about 95 qps across 2 nodes at 512 tokens, avg token cost X (we put exacts in the sheet). with continuous-batching + 20ms we hit ~255 qps evenly distributed, roughly 2.6x. p50 went from 120ms to 150ms, p95 from 480ms to 420ms under controlled concurrency.

04:36 Speaker 4 (Carlos): so if traffic is bursty we lose that p95 benefit?

04:44 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes if you allow unconstrained concurrent requests, queueing increases and the p95 climbs because late requests wait in batch queue longer. that's why we recommend a two-tier approach: a concurrency knob to protect latency SLOs and a queue-depth threshold to apply backpressure or route to a lower-cost model variant.

05:05 Speaker 2 (Priya): can you route to a smaller quantized model automatically when spikes happen? that's interesting for cost control.

05:13 Speaker 3 (Liam): absolutely — Redwood's smart routing supports model variants and fallbacks. on capacity events you can prefer a low-precision quantized variant with similar output quality for non-critical paths; we can tune the policy to keep critical payment flows on the high-accuracy model.

05:28 Speaker 6 (Kenji): what's the impact on inference output when we go to int8 quantized variants? we've had some hallucination concerns earlier.

05:35 Speaker 3 (Liam): in our internal evals the particular family you're using retained >98% BLEU/ROUGE-style similarity for shorter prompts, but for long-context generation there can be small regressions. that's why we suggest a routing policy tied to evals: run a few thousand representative prompts and measure degradation and only route lower-criticality requests.

05:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay quick pause — does everyone have the latest benchmark link? i shared the google sheet in the chat earlier.

06:06 Speaker 2 (Priya): got it.

06:12 Speaker 4 (Susan): i skimmed and saw notes about sequence length distribution — our production median is 220 tokens, 95th is 680 tokens. does your continuous-batching tuning change with that distribution?

06:26 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes, longer sequences reduce per-token throughput because KV cache warmup and attention compute grow quadratically. for your distribution the gains from batching are slightly less at the 95th but still material. we tuned batch_target down to 96 for mixed length runs to avoid excessive queuing for long tails.

06:46 Speaker 2 (Priya): ok that maps, curious about the concurrency-cap suggestion of 40 per node — feels arbitrary. how did you derive that?

06:55 Speaker 3 (Liam): it's empirical: from stress tests with your model we measured the knee where p95 jumps; below 40 per node p95 stays under your 500ms SLO for most loads. above that you hit memory/queue contention. we can provide a graph in the sheet.

07:18 Speaker 4 (Carlos): can Redwood provide automated scaling so we can keep concurrency under the knee during peaks?

07:27 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes — Dedicated autoscaling can spin up extra nodes based on queue depth and per-node concurrency. for hosted customers we have similar autoscale but without reserved capacity there can be transient cold-starts.

07:42 Speaker 6 (Kenji): cold-starts are a hard no for some flows. we'll need warm pools for high-priority endpoints.

07:50 Speaker 1 (Maya): noted, we'll put warm pool sizing options in the pricing doc.

08:00 Speaker 4 (Susan): security question — are logs/audit trails for every inference available? we need auditability for payments.

08:08 Speaker 5 (Avery): yes, Redwood Private/Dedicated includes audit logs and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management. we'll attach the SOC2 and audit docs but the private option gives you the control plane in your VPC.

08:22 Speaker 2 (Priya): on the bench runs you said there were some transcription glitches in the logs where model names got messed up — is that relevant to reproducibility?

08:30 Speaker 3 (Liam): just a note, our transcription of the run summaries is sometimes noisy; the raw benchmark CSV has machine-measured latency/throughput per sample, that's the authoritative source.

08:43 Speaker 4 (Carlos): can we talk about queueing policies — do you let the queue grow or reject early when backpressure happens? we prefer predictable failures over big latency spikes.

08:53 Speaker 3 (Liam): good question. recommended policy: apply per-route queue-length cap + priority queuing. critical payment paths have a small queue and overflow should be rejected with 429 so the caller can retry with jitter. non-critical batch jobs can be queued deeper and drained.

09:12 Speaker 6 (Kenji): that aligns with our ops model. what's the recommended retry/backoff pattern? too aggressive retries can amplify thundering herd.

09:22 Speaker 3 (Liam): exponential backoff with randomized jitter, and a max retry window of ~500ms for user interactive flows. plus client-side rate limiting is helpful. we'll share sample client libs config.

09:38 Speaker 2 (Priya): for the next run, can you also include a run with batch_timeout 50ms so we can see the max throughput point vs latency tradeoff?

09:48 Speaker 3 (Liam): yes we ran 50ms locally — throughput rose to ~310 qps but p50 increased to ~200ms and p95 to ~560ms under bursty conditions. we'll include those rows.

10:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): any blockers on the legal/security side for a Private deployment?

10:11 Speaker 4 (Susan): we're fine with the standard NDA, but will want SOC2 and evidence of encryption in transit and at rest. also need to know where logs live — residency requirements.

10:23 Speaker 5 (Avery): understood. we'll attach SOC2 report and a brief on our KMS integrations. residency is configurable for Dedicated/Private — we'll note the supported regions.

10:33 Speaker 2 (Priya): ok last item — what's the ask from NovaPay for the on-site run? we need to prep infra and security access.

10:41 Speaker 3 (Liam): ideal: provide a staging VPC with 2 nodes same size as prod, shared creds for a timebox, and a list of representative prompt sets. we'll run a ramp test and then a 1-hour soak.

10:54 Speaker 4 (Carlos): we'll carve out a staging window and get Kenji to coordinate. can we do the on-site run the week of 8/11?

11:02 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes that's what we penciled in. final recap — Liam to share the updated CSV and graphs, Maya to share configs and pricing, Carlos to confirm staging window and provide SLOs, Priya to provide representative prompt set. action items in the chat.

11:22 Speaker 2 (Priya): thanks everyone, productive as always.

11:28 Speaker 1 (Maya): great, we'll follow up by EOD with docs.

End of transcript.
